title: How can each length be written in two ways?
description: A USB cable of four units and eight tenths is written first as units and tenths and then as one count of tenths. Four numbers are read aloud, and a hand, a box and a leaf are each written in two ways. Keeko doubts the cable and adds the four units to the eight tenths.
teaching_notes: One idea: a length of units and tenths becomes one count of tenths by multiplying the units by ten and adding the tenths. Watch for students who add the units to the tenths and say twelve tenths.

source: A USB cable is 4 8/10 units long. Write it in two ways. Then read aloud 4 1/10, 4/10, 41/10 and 41 1/10. Three more objects are drawn on their own unit scales: a hand that reaches 1 unit and 6 tenths, a box that is 2 units and 3 tenths, and a leaf that is 3 units and 9 tenths. Write each of these in two ways.
video_script.why: The child can turn units and tenths into one count of tenths for one length and now does it for four lengths and reads such numbers aloud.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the units by ten and add the tenths to get the count of tenths.
video_script.anchor: A USB cable of four units and eight tenths on a bar cut into tenths, with a hand, a box and a leaf on their own unit scales
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the 4 units to the 8 tenths to get 4 + 8 = 12 tenths, but 4 units are 40 tenths, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The cable is four and eight tenths, which is forty eight tenths

final_answer.spoken: the cable is forty eight tenths, the hand is sixteen tenths, the box is twenty three tenths, and the leaf is thirty nine tenths

maths_rules: USB cable: 4 units and 8 tenths is 4 8/10, and 4 × 10 + 8 = 48 tenths, so 48/10.
Reading: 4 1/10 is four and one tenth; 4/10 is four tenths; 41/10 is forty one tenths; 41 1/10 is forty one and one tenth.
Slip: 4 + 8 = 12 tenths, but 4 units are 40 tenths.
video_script.design: One idea: a length of units and tenths is also one count of tenths, found by multiplying the units by ten and adding the tenths. Assumes ten tenths make one unit. Wrong idea: add the units to the tenths. The hand, box and leaf lengths are the ones in the book's figures and are not in the extracted text. The USB bar stays all video.
open_questions: The hand, box and leaf lengths (1 6/10, 2 3/10, 3 9/10) come from the worklist; the book text gives only the figures, so check them against the figure.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the cable is twelve tenths, because four and eight make twelve.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four whole units are already forty tenths, far more than twelve. A unit is not one tenth. A unit is ten tenths.
